standard_prerequisites.use: Closedness of the locus of bounded fibre dimension (Morphisms), and the two spreading lemmas for closed sets with empty or nonempty generic fibre (same chapter); cited inputs, with both shrinking steps written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Define Z as the locus where the local fibre dimension exceeds n and deduce from the cited lemma that Z is closed in X.
Note Z has empty fibre over the generic point and shrink the base once so that Z is empty everywhere.
Define Z' as the locus of fibre dimension at least n, check it is closed and meets the generic fibre.
Shrink the base so that Z' -> Y is surjective, giving dim of every fibre exactly n over the retained open.

proof_roadmap.step: Kill the locus of too-large fibre dimension using closedness and the empty-generic-fibre shrinking lemma.
Force the locus of dimension at least n to dominate by shrinking, and conclude.

difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism onto an irreducible base whose generic fibre has dimension n, one must produce one nonempty open of the base over which every fibre has dimension exactly n. The proof handles the upper and lower bounds with two closed loci: the locus where the local fibre dimension exceeds n, closed by the openness-of-bounded-dimension lemma and killed over the generic point, hence removable after shrinking; and the locus of dimension at least n, which meets the generic fibre, hence becomes surjective after shrinking. Both shrinking moves are written out with their lemmas. Retained author proof at lines 8419-8432.
